data.title: bn-1yya: rite channel serves mentions into a Claude Code session as an MCP channel server

data.body: [risk:high] Default channel startup fails open when session attachment cannot acquire the agent identity. Lines 123-126 log the error and continue with no attachment, and tests/channel.rs:221-245 requires continued service. The process can then stream and reply as the same agent beside the existing holder. Lines 134-139 also ignore renew failure and keep serving after occupancy is lost. Failure modes: duplicate responders and conflicting replies under one identity. Edge cases: an identity already held, damaged claim or session logs, an expired claim with a competing holder, or a renew interval longer than the eight-hour attachment TTL. Rollback: stop this server and detach only its owned attachment. Never release the competing claim. Monitoring: treat missing attachment and any renew error as terminal, and expose readiness. Validation: assert startup exits before MCP initialization when attach fails. Force claim loss during renew and assert the server closes and cannot call reply.

[risk:high] Occupancy is acquired before MCP channel readiness and is not coupled to stream health. The stream starts only after notifications/initialized, while lines 232-234 only log stream termination. The independent renewal thread can therefore suppress the responder while no message path exists. Failure modes: incoming work is silently stranded behind a healthy occupancy claim. Edge cases: no initialized notification, a policy-disabled channel, watcher setup failure, watcher termination, a closed stdout pipe, or a client that leaves stdin open. Rollback: detach this attachment and exit the server without changing unrelated claims. Monitoring: publish a ready state only after stream setup, track the stream task, and treat output failures as loss of delivery. Validation: launch without notifications/initialized and verify no long-lived claim. Inject watcher failure and closed stdout while stdin stays open, then assert detach and exit.

[risk:high] Abandoned pre-launch reservations are reconciled only when another session command calls this function. After pending_until, agent_is_reserved stops blocking on the session record, but the owner-bound agent claim remains active until its much longer TTL. Generic claim release also skips it. A crashed launcher with defaults can therefore suppress a responder for eight hours instead of the ten-minute reservation window. Failure modes: cold-spawn denial and stranded work after a launcher crash. Edge cases: crash after reserve but before bind, no later session command, ordinary hook traffic, and custom long claim TTLs. Rollback: conditionally detach or reconcile the abandoned attachment and release only its owned claim. Monitoring: report abandoned pending records that still own live claims, including remaining claim TTL. Validation: reserve with a short window and long TTL, age the pending record past the window, trigger a claim-gated hook without any session command, and assert the hook can acquire occupancy after safe reconciliation.

data.reason: Three risk:high blockers remain: fail-open identity attachment and renewal, occupancy without a healthy delivery stream, and abandoned reservations that retain owner-bound claims beyond their window.

data.body: [risk:high] BLOCK remains. src/cli/channel.rs:180-186 arms the stream before attach_and_renew runs. src/cli/channel.rs:248-260 starts the follow loop as soon as readiness is signaled, so it can emit a mention while the attach subprocess still waits, or before that subprocess reports a competing holder. src/cli/channel.rs:289-300 also stores the attachment id only after attach returns, so stream or stdout failure in that interval exits without detaching the claim that was just acquired. Failure modes: a second session can receive and answer work before identity exclusion succeeds, or a failed startup can strand its owned claim. Edge cases: claims-lock contention, a slow competing-holder failure, a mention immediately after stream readiness, and stdout or watcher loss between child attach success and attachment publication. Rollback: stop the channel server and detach only its recorded attachment. Do not release a competing claim. Monitoring: expose stream-armed, occupancy-held, and delivery-enabled separately, and reject any delivery before all required states are true. Validation: hold the claims lock to pause attach, send a mention after initialization, and assert no notification until successful occupancy. Repeat with a competing holder and assert no notification. Force output or stream loss after child attach success but before publication, then assert the owned claim is detached.
[risk:high] Verified the direct repair at src/cli/channel.rs:289-307. Attach failure and renewal failure now terminate the server. The remaining startup ordering defect is tracked in th-zop7un.

data.reason: Direct attach and renew fail-open paths are repaired. Remaining delivery ordering defect stays open in th-zop7un.

data.body: [risk:high] Verified the local repair at src/cli/hooks.rs:1006-1016 and src/cli/sessions.rs:372-437. Hook admission detects an abandoned reservation, reconciles its owner-bound claim, and rechecks reservation state under the claim lock.

data.reason: Local abandoned reservations are reconciled during hook admission with conditional owner-bound release.

[risk:high] src/cli/channel.rs:180-186 and 248-300 enable delivery before occupancy is secured and can lose the attachment id during startup failure. Keep th-zop7un open. The risk:critical human-approval gate remains separate and unsatisfied.

data.body: [risk:high][still-open] Runtime watcher failure remains fail-open. src/cli/channel.rs:297-309 shuts down only when follow_with_ready returns. src/storage/watch.rs:45-54 discards notify errors and converts receiver disconnection into empty batches, so follow_with_ready spins forever while renewals keep agent:// held. Failure modes: a dead watcher suppresses cold responders while no mentions arrive. Edge cases: a permanent notify backend error, a disconnected callback channel, or directory watch invalidation after readiness. Rollback: detach only this server attachment and exit. Monitoring: surface watcher errors and disconnection as terminal, and expose stream health. Validation: inject a notify error and receiver disconnect after attachment, then assert server exit, attachment detach, and claim release.

[risk:high] The activation handoff can strand a mention permanently. Lines 90-96 drain buffered under the mutex, unlock, and only then set delivering. A concurrent deliver that read false before the store can acquire the mutex after the drain and append an event that no later path flushes. Failure modes: one accepted mention is silently lost while occupancy remains healthy. Edge cases: mention arrival during attach completion or while earlier buffered events flush. Rollback: detach this attachment and exit so another responder can recover later work. The lost mention needs manual replay. Monitoring: count buffered, flushed, and post-activation buffered records, and treat a nonzero residual as failure. Validation: use a barrier after deliver reads false and before it locks. Activate delivery, release the barrier, and assert the exact message is emitted once.

[risk:high] The reply tool is callable without occupancy. Lines 240-253 execute reply for every tools/call even before notifications/initialized, while attachment begins only at lines 228-235. A second or broken client can write bus messages as the same agent while another holder owns agent://. Failure modes: duplicate or conflicting replies under one identity. Edge cases: calls after initialize but before initialized, a competing holder, attach failure, or calls during shutdown. Rollback: stop this server. Do not release the competing holder. Monitoring: reject and log calls until delivery and occupancy are confirmed, and after shutdown begins. Validation: call reply before initialized and with a competing holder, then assert no bus write. Repeat after successful attach and assert one anchored write.

[risk:medium] Pre-occupancy buffering silently deletes the oldest records after 1000 entries. A delayed attach can cross this cap while the mention cursor advances, so deleted events never replay. Keep a bounded buffer, but make overflow terminal or auditable and recoverable.

data.reason: Three risk:high defects remain: runtime watcher loss retains occupancy without delivery, delivery activation can strand a buffered mention, and reply calls bypass occupancy before readiness. The risk:medium buffer-overflow loss also remains. This BLOCK does not satisfy or waive the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.body: [risk:high][still-open] Runtime watcher failure remains fail-open at the exact target. src/storage/watch.rs:45-54 discards backend errors and receiver disconnection, so src/cli/mentions.rs:318-372 keeps looping while src/cli/channel.rs:378-383 renews agent:// occupancy. Failure modes: delivery dies while cold responders remain suppressed. Edge cases: notify overflow, directory invalidation, permanent backend error, or callback disconnect. Rollback: stop this server and detach only its exact attachment. Monitoring: surface watcher health and make every error or disconnect terminal. Validation: inject each failure after attachment and assert server exit, detach, and claim release. Initial watcher setup errors propagate at src/cli/mentions.rs:292-293, but runtime failures do not.

[risk:high][new blocker] Reply authorization has a teardown race. src/cli/channel.rs:117-119 checks two atomics once, then src/cli/channel.rs:262-274 starts a synchronous rite send without lifecycle fencing. A renewal or stream thread can set stopping, detach at src/cli/channel.rs:123-160, and exit while the orphaned send child later appends the reply. Failure modes: a reply is written after identity occupancy is lost, possibly beside a successor. Edge cases: slow send, claims contention, renewal failure, or delivery loss during tools/call. Rollback: stop the server and inspect the affected thread; do not release a successor claim. Monitoring: record in-flight replies and reject teardown until they finish or are cancelled. Validation: pause after may_reply, force shutdown and successor occupancy, then release the send and assert no message is written. The pre-occupancy tests at tests/channel.rs:102-118 do not cover concurrent teardown.

[risk:high] Overflow shutdown can orphan the synchronous attach child. src/cli/channel.rs:90-95 can call shutdown while src/cli/channel.rs:349-364 waits in Command::output. If cleanup at src/cli/channel.rs:148-155 runs before src/cli/sessions.rs:869 writes the pending record, detach is a no-op. process::exit then leaves the child free to commit at src/cli/sessions.rs:958. Failure modes: a dead channel owns agent:// and suppresses responders for its claim TTL. Edge cases: a burst above 1000 eligible mentions during session-lock, claim-lock, or large-log delay. Rollback: find and detach the orphaned attachment. Monitoring: track attach child PID, reservation, commit, and parent liveness. Validation: pause the child before line 869, overflow the buffer, release it, and assert no attachment or claim survives. Normal shutdown after attachment publication uses the exact id, but tests do not cover pre-reservation parent exit.

[risk:high] Reconciliation can release occupancy acquired after its stale session snapshot. src/cli/sessions.rs:398-402 records reserved owners, then lines 405-433 release a later claim owner absent from that snapshot. release_owned at src/cli/sessions.rs:207-220 rechecks only claim ownership, not whether the owner became reserved. Failure modes: a replacement loses occupancy, cannot commit, and cannot hand the inactive claim back; the predecessor remains attached without its claim. Edge cases: concurrent reserve, direct attach, or attach --replace during abandoned-record reconciliation. Rollback: renew the predecessor or detach and retry the successor. Monitoring: flag every attached session whose occupancy is not held. Validation: pause reconciliation after line 402, transfer ownership concurrently, resume, and assert the claim remains held. Local hook admission also checks session reservations, which limits immediate duplicate spawning, but it does not preserve the occupancy invariant.

[risk:high] Sync does not enforce the new host-local boundary on pull or direct push. src/sync/git.rs:245-268 removes local only during sync commit, but src/sync/git.rs:297-343 pushes HEAD unchanged and lines 346-425 merge every remote path. A tracked remote local/sessions.jsonl therefore materializes despite .gitignore. Valid attached or unknown records reserve identities at src/core/session.rs:398-403, and malformed content makes agent_is_reserved fail closed at lines 355-367. Failure modes: imported stale routing state, responder denial, session-id disclosure, or local-state replacement. Edge cases: upgraded stores, historical or manual commits, malformed logs, and tracked remote paths. Rollback: stop sync, preserve the real local log, remove local from remote history or tree, then restore host-local state. Monitoring: reject or warn on git ls-files and origin trees containing local. Validation: use two clones and prove pull leaves local bytes unchanged and push refuses tracked local state. New repositories ignore local and sync commit untracks it, but neither control protects pull or direct push.

data.reason: BLOCK: five risk:high blockers remain at 796f9e968586db63b22eb46845e5f2a98f0e98a6: runtime watcher failure keeps occupancy, reply teardown can outlive occupancy, overflow shutdown can orphan attach, reconciliation can release newly acquired occupancy, and sync can import or export host-local sessions. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.

Failure modes: silent message stranding and responder suppression. Edge cases: notify overflow, invalidation, backend failure, disconnect. data.body: [risk:high] Stream failure can still orphan the direct attach child before its reservation is visible. src/cli/channel.rs:351-363 lets the watcher thread enter shutdown while src/cli/channel.rs:376-398 is blocked in Command::output. With attachment still unset, src/cli/channel.rs:142-168 launches detach by session, but src/cli/sessions.rs:1134-1166 treats a session absent from its snapshot as a successful no-op. If that detach wins the snapshot race before the attach child appends its pending record at src/cli/sessions.rs:918-942, process::exit does not terminate the independent child; it can later occupy and commit at src/cli/sessions.rs:995-1019, leaving a dead channel holding agent:// for at least one hour. Failure modes: an unreachable session suppresses responders and addressed work is stranded. Edge cases: a watcher backend error or disconnect immediately after readiness, claims or sessions lock contention, and slow sync auto-commit before attach returns. Rollback: detach the orphan by its known session id or attachment id; release only its owned claim. Monitoring: record attach-child PID and phase, parent liveness, and any attached stream session without a live channel process. Validation: deterministically pause direct attach before its first session append, inject watcher failure, let detach observe no record, allow parent exit, then release the child and assert no attached record or claim survives. Coordinate all shutdown causes with attach completion, or reserve first so cleanup always has a durable attachment id.

[risk:high] Push-at-send does not require the selected attachment to hold occupancy. src/cli/sessions.rs:1560-1598 selects every attached push session from local state, then src/cli/sessions.rs:1641-1676 executes its adapter without loading claims or checking that agent:// is still unexpired and owned by that attachment. After renewal stops or ownership changes, a sender can continue injecting work into the stale session even though exclusivity is lost; an older hook, a manual claimant, or another version can then act as the same agent. Failure modes: duplicate processing and conflicting replies under one identity. Edge cases: claim expiry, release or transfer after the session snapshot, a stale attached record after bridge failure, and mixed-version hooks that only inspect claims. Rollback: stop push delivery to the stale attachment and explicitly detach it if its harness is confirmed gone; do not release a successor claim. Monitoring: report and reject any push whose attachment occupancy is not held, and correlate delivery with attachment and claim owner. Validation: attach a push session with a short TTL, let its claim lapse or transfer it to a successor, send an addressed message, and assert the stale adapter is never invoked. Re-check under the claims lock immediately before spawn if exclusivity is a delivery precondition.

data.reason: Two risk:high blockers remain at 7175b5f: attach teardown can orphan its child before the session reservation exists, and push-at-send can invoke a stale attachment without current occupancy.

data.body: [risk:high][verified-fixed] Target 8943c737a353f2f7a8097b0ce87ee4ed28423a5e closes the completing-child orphan race. src/cli/channel.rs:146-176 makes shutdown wait for attach_gate before choosing detach identity, while src/cli/channel.rs:385-415 holds that gate from before child spawn through storage of the exact attachment id. Shutdown therefore sees either no started attach or the completed attachment id.

data.body: [risk:high][still-open at 8943c737a353f2f7a8097b0ce87ee4ed28423a5e] Push occupancy validation is not fenced through adapter spawn. src/cli/sessions.rs:1646-1655 checks the owned unexpired claim inside with_exclusive_read, but src/storage/jsonl.rs:375-376 releases that lock before run_push is called at src/cli/sessions.rs:1670-1679 and before Command::spawn at src/cli/sessions.rs:1797-1799. Failure modes: detach, replacement, or expiry can remove occupancy after the check and the stale session still receives work beside a successor. Edge cases: concurrent detach, ownership transfer, claim expiry at the validation boundary, and a delayed adapter spawn. Rollback: stop delivery to the stale attachment and detach only the confirmed stale session; do not release a successor claim. Monitoring: correlate each adapter spawn with the claim owner and expiry at its linearization point. Validation: pause after the locked check returns, detach or replace the attachment, resume, and assert that the stale adapter is never spawned.

[risk:high] Reserve can report success after its reservation is already dead. src/cli/sessions.rs:650-657 appends the pending record, src/cli/sessions.rs:672-681 acquires occupancy, and src/cli/sessions.rs:693-726 returns success without rechecking that pending state. A zero-second window reaches this through ordinary CLI input; lock or auto-commit delay and concurrent detach also reach it. Failure modes: the launcher starts a harness without durable exclusion, or a ghost claim blocks delivery. Edge cases: --window 0, short windows, claims-lock contention, slow Git auto-commit, and detach between reserve append and occupy. Rollback: stop the unbound harness, retire the exact reservation, and release only its owned claim. Monitoring: flag successful reserve responses whose attachment is not still pending and whose claim is not owned and live. Validation: pause after the session append or use a zero window, let the reservation retire or lapse, resume, and assert reserve fails with no surviving claim.

[risk:high] Buffer overflow is not atomically coupled to activation. src/cli/channel.rs:103-110 drops the over-cap event and sets overflowed, but src/cli/channel.rs:280-286 checks that flag before enable_delivery takes the buffer lock. A delivery that fills the cap between those operations is dropped, after which delivery is enabled and the server stays live. Failure modes: one accepted mention is silently lost while occupancy remains healthy. Edge cases: the buffer reaching exactly 1000 during attach completion, burst delivery, and scheduler delay between the overflow check and activation. Rollback: detach this channel attachment, restart it, and recover the lost message from inbox. Monitoring: count buffered, overflowed, flushed, and residual records and treat every overflow as terminal. Validation: place a barrier after the flag check, deliver the over-cap event, then resume activation and assert the server exits and releases its exact claim.

[risk:high] Cursor continuity is inferred only from file length. src/cli/mentions.rs:225-230 resets only when a changed channel shrinks; src/cli/mentions.rs:352-362 reads an equal-size or larger replacement from the stale byte offset and advances past missed or partial data. rite channel then keeps renewing occupancy without delivering the skipped mention. Failure modes: addressed work is silently stranded while cold responders remain suppressed. Edge cases: Git sync or restore rewriting a channel, atomic replacement, and coalesced delete plus recreate at equal or greater length. Rollback: detach the exact channel attachment, restart the follower, and recover missed work from the durable inbox. Monitoring: track file identity and prefix continuity, and make any cursor reset or mismatch visible. Validation: replace a watched file with different valid JSONL of equal or greater length and assert a full rescan delivers each new message exactly once.

[risk:medium] sync init with a remote bypasses the host-local history gate for case variants. src/sync/git.rs:69-72 ignores only lowercase local, src/sync/git.rs:109-130 stages existing JSONL recursively, and src/sync/git.rs:145-149 pushes directly instead of using the guarded path at src/sync/git.rs:310-327. On a case-sensitive host, pre-existing LOCAL/sessions.jsonl is therefore committed and published even though src/sync/git.rs:487-503 defines case variants as host-local. This can disclose session identifiers and requires remote history rewriting. Apply the same case-insensitive tree and outgoing-history checks before the initialization push, and cover init with a pre-existing case-variant local tree.

data.reason: Four risk:high blockers remain: push validation is not fenced through adapter spawn; reserve can succeed after its pending record dies; mention cursors lose equal-size or larger file replacements; and buffer overflow can race activation and remain non-terminal. data.body: [risk:high][still-open at 93b5a8d826a118509a106b2006f9be8a6556c3f3] The cursor does not prove full prefix continuity. src/cli/mentions.rs:192-207 retains only the last 4096 bytes, and src/cli/mentions.rs:267-285 trusts the old offset when that tail, inode, and minimum length match. An in-place rewrite can insert or replace a mention earlier than offset minus 4096 while preserving the suffix, so the follower resumes at the stale offset and never scans it. Failure modes: addressed work is silently stranded while this channel keeps agent occupancy. Edge cases: a large channel restored with cp, an in-place merge, or any rewrite that changes only an early record and preserves the trailing 4 KiB. Rollback: stop and detach the exact channel session, restart from durable history, and manually recover the missed message. Monitoring: report every rewrite decision and bind the cursor to a digest of the complete consumed prefix or another durable continuity token. Validation: build a file larger than 8 KiB, preserve its final 4 KiB and inode, insert a fresh mention before that window, then assert a reset and exactly one delivery. The current in-place test at src/cli/mentions.rs:759-805 is smaller than the fingerprint window.

[risk:high] A skipped partial record advances the live cursor past data that can later become valid. src/cli/mentions.rs:450-460 treats read_messages_from_offset as successful and always records new_offset. src/storage/jsonl.rs:612-644 records parse failures but still returns Ok with the offset after the malformed bytes. If an unlocked in-place restore is observed mid-line, the first read skips the prefix and advances to its temporary EOF. The next read starts inside the completed JSON record, skips the suffix, and loses that mention permanently. Failure modes: one addressed message never reaches the occupied channel session. Edge cases: cp or restore into the watched inode, sync tooling that does not honor the JSONL lock, and recovery of a crash-torn final line. Rollback: detach and restart the follower, then recover the message from durable inbox history. Monitoring: make skipped incremental records terminal or retain the first skipped byte offset until a clean reread succeeds. Validation: pause an in-place writer after half a JSONL mention, let the watcher drain it, finish the same line, and assert the exact message arrives once without another unrelated write.

[risk:high] A separately observed delete erases the deduplication history and makes a restored channel replay old work. src/cli/mentions.rs:442-447 calls forget when the path is absent, and src/cli/mentions.rs:312-317 removes both the offset and every seen message id. When the same channel file returns, src/cli/mentions.rs:267-270 starts at zero and src/cli/mentions.rs:307-310 treats all prior ids as new. Failure modes: previously processed requests can run again and produce duplicate changes or replies. Edge cases: a slow delete-then-restore across two debounce windows, a channel renamed away and back, or sync software that briefly removes the path. Rollback: stop and detach the channel session, inspect replayed message ids, and reverse duplicate side effects manually. Monitoring: retain a durable per-channel high-water identity across temporary absence and report replay attempts. Validation: seed history, deliver one live mention, let one watcher batch observe the file absent, restore the original file plus a new mention, and assert only the new id is emitted.

Fixed at 4b3ae04: send --id sweeps every other channel for the id (offset_after_message_id) and appends to the destination via append_if under its exclusive lock, refusing an id already present. Test a_reused_message_id_is_refused_at_the_append covers same-channel and cross-channel reuse.

data.body: [risk:high][not-fixed] The cross-channel uniqueness check remains non-atomic. src/cli/send.rs:517-535 takes and releases each other channel shared lock. It later acquires only the destination lock at src/cli/send.rs:283-287. Two concurrent sends can sweep different destinations before either append. Both then append the same caller-supplied ID. Failure modes: duplicate IDs silently suppress mentions and make thread, lookup, and deletion identity ambiguous. Edge cases: simultaneous same-ID sends to two existing or newly created channels. Rollback: stop followers, audit every channel for duplicate IDs, repair records, then restart from a verified baseline. Monitoring: make doctor report store-wide duplicate IDs and reject collisions before success. Validation: synchronize two send processes after their cross-channel sweeps and before destination appends, then require exactly one failure. Use one store-wide ID fence or another atomic uniqueness authority.
